findings.summary: Regression from F2: in fi and sv, an inch or foot mark inside a quotation set in curly ”…” or ’…’ now becomes that quotation’s closing mark. Counting ” and ’ as openers makes openD/openS non-zero, closerAhead() returns false for a pair whose two marks are the same glyph, and the single-quote digit branch has no curly-closer test at all, so the digit branch takes D_CLOSE. c3b3b49 gave the prime. The page pass and fix on save write it, and the second pass cannot repair it.

findings.acceptance: Inside a fi/sv curly quotation, a straight " or ' after a digit is a prime unless it is the quotation’s end, as before F2: for a same-glyph pair, a matching mark still to come after the token (counted as closerAhead counts, a ’ only where no letter or digit follows) makes it a prime, and the single digit branch gets the same test. Corpus cases for the six inputs above give ″ / ′ in typed and depth, and a case where the mark is the real closer (”Det är 5" → ”Det är 5”) still closes. Re-running recheck-r7v2/basediff.mjs shows no fi/sv row where c3b3b49 gave a prime and HEAD does not.
findings.cause: F2 made ” and ’ count as openers without extending FU5’s curly-closer-ahead test to pairs whose marks are one glyph.
